chunks: And from him (Al-Shaykh) from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from Abu al-Subah al-Kinanī from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When a man has sexual intercourse with a woman, her daughter does not become permanently forbidden to him, even if he had previously married the daughter and had not yet consummated the marriage with her; in that case, his marriage to the daughter is annulled. And if he married the daughter, consummated the marriage with her, and then had sexual intercourse with her mother after having consummated the marriage with the daughter, his sexual intercourse with the mother does not invalidate the marriage to the daughter, provided he had already consummated it with her."
And this is his saying: 'That which makes something forbidden does not invalidate the permissible, if it is thus.'

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: He entered with her (consummated the marriage)
key_terms.فَجَرَ: To have sexual intercourse (specifically outside of marriage or in a context creating prohibition)

ai.seo_question: Does sexual intercourse with a mother invalidate the marriage to her daughter in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* elucidates the principle of *la yufsidu al-haram al-halal* (illicit act does not invalidate the licit) by distinguishing between permanent and temporary marital bonds based on consummation. It establishes that while intercourse with a mother creates a permanent barrier to her daughter, it only annuls a daughter's marriage if that union remains unconsummated at the time of the act. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the physical consummation (*dukhul*) as the decisive factor for the stability of the marital bond in cases of concurrent illicit relations.
